captions.gbp:
Did your mammogram results letter say you have dense breasts? You're not alone: about half of women 40 and older have dense breast tissue, and since September 2024 federal (FDA) rules require every mammogram letter to say whether your tissue is dense. Dense means your breasts have more glandular and fibrous tissue than fat. It's normal, not a disease, and you can't feel it. It can make a mammogram harder to read, because dense tissue and tumors both look white, and it modestly raises breast cancer risk as one factor among several. A 3D mammogram looks at breast tissue layer by layer, and depending on your overall risk your doctor may suggest a breast ultrasound or MRI. Experts don't yet agree on extra tests for dense breasts, so talk with your doctor about what's right for you. Advanced Medical Imaging offers 3D mammograms and breast ultrasound in Seminole. Coverage varies by plan.

Book online at advancedimg.com. General information, not medical advice.

facts_checked: Checked 2026-10-16. FDA 'Understanding Breast Density': approximately half of women over 40 have dense tissue; patient letter must say dense or not dense, effective September 2024; dense tissue can hide cancers and is a risk factor; other imaging may help some. CDC 'About Dense Breasts': about half of women 40+; density is not how breasts feel or look; ultrasound and MRI may find some cancers mammograms miss, with false positives and possible lack of coverage. ACS 'Breast Density and Your Mammogram Report': categories A to D; dense tissue and cancer both look white; 3D may help in dense breasts; experts do not agree on supplemental tests. USPSTF 2024: I statement (insufficient evidence) for supplemental screening in dense breasts. Practice facts from amiweb 5822719: services-data.ts mammography (Hologic 3D, Seminole, breast ultrasound $195 self-pay), lp/mammogram-ultrasound-seminole-fl, constants.ts phone and hours.
